Paragraph:
Translation: O Dhananjaya, rid yourself of all fruitive activities by devotional service, and surrender fully to that consciousness. Those who want to enjoy the fruits of their work are misers.

Purport (Excerpt): Only misers desire to enjoy the fruit of their own work just to be further entangled in material bondage. Except for work in Krsna consciousness, all activities are abominable because they continually bind the worker to the cycle of birth and death... Misers do not know how to utilize the assets of riches which they acquire... One should spend all energies working in Krsna consciousness...
Situation/Problem_Faced: The default human condition is to work entirely for selfish acquisition, believing that hoarding the results of our labor will bring security and happiness.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna flips the societal definition of wealth. He calls those who work only for their own enjoyment 'misers' (kripana). True expansiveness of consciousness comes from dedicating one's work to a higher, selfless purpose.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna's worldview is challenged to shift from a narrow, ego-centric 'scarcity mindset' to a broad, service-oriented 'abundance mindset'.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Scarcity vs. Abundance Mindset: Moving from 'what can I keep for myself' to 'how can I serve the whole'
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Purpose-Driven Action: Finding deeper meaning beyond a paycheck or personal glory
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Ego Reduction: Decreasing the obsessive focus on 'I, me, and mine'

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Kripana (A miser; one who wastes the rare opportunity of human life on petty, selfish gains)
Buddhi-yoga (Working with intelligence aligned with the Supreme)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Working merely to gratify one's own senses guarantees continued suffering and karmic entanglement. A spiritually intelligent person utilizes their energy, talents, and resources as offerings to the Divine, unlike a 'miser' who selfishly hoards them and misses the true value of human life.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: This concept targets the exhaustion of the 'rat race.' When an individual acts solely for personal gain, they operate from a place of psychological poverty and insecurity (the 'miser'). This leads to burnout. By reframing work as an act of service or devotion, we tap into a deeper well of motivation, reducing the ego's constant anxiety over 'getting mine.'
